review.tagline: Terminal coding agent with build and plan modes, plus a desktop app
review.summary: OpenCode is an AI coding agent that runs in the terminal and as a beta desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux. It ships a full-access build agent, a read-only plan agent that asks before running bash commands, and a general subagent invoked with @general. It installs through a curl script, npm, Homebrew, Scoop, Chocolatey, pacman, mise or nix.
review.audience: Developers who want an open source coding agent in the terminal or desktop
strengths: Read-only plan agent denies file edits by default and asks before bash commands
Many install paths: curl script, npm, brew, scoop, choco, pacman, mise, nix
Switch between build and plan agents with the Tab key
MIT licensed, with desktop installers for macOS, Windows and Linux
weaknesses: README does not list supported model providers or formats
README gives no hardware requirements; configuration is only in external docs
Primary install command pipes a curl script into bash
